d.why: On screen in three season 6 episodes of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (The Other Thing, Inescapable, From the Ashes).
Only in Aftershocks (mentioned in The Frenemy of My Enemy), but he is the target of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s ruse: the Hydra head who hosts the meeting, orders his rivals killed and is shot by Hunter.
On screen in two season 7 episodes (The End is at Hand, What We're Fighting For).
Only in The Bridge, where he is one of the Centipede soldiers who break Po out and is killed through his implant; a henchman in the Po and Mike Peterson story, and his sister Laura has no file.
On screen in three season 4 Framework episodes (Self Control, What If..., No Regrets).
On screen in seven season 4 episodes (4x03 and 4x05 to 4x10) as Mace's image handler.
Only in The New Deal (mentioned later), but he is one of the episode's Chronicom Hunter villains: he tries to kill Quake, is captured, and his meltdown under questioning gives up Malick's name.
Only in T.R.A.C.K.S., where he guards Ian Quinn's package on the train, fits the leg on Mike and is killed; a guard in Quinn's story, with no family or subordinate who has a file.

Only in Spacetime, an episode that turns on him (Daisy tries to stop the death his touch showed her, and he dies saving her), and he is the husband of Polly Hinton and father of Robin Hinton, who both have files.
On screen in three season 4 Framework episodes (Self Control, What If..., No Regrets).
Only in The Totally Excellent Adventures of Mack and the D, where he finds Mack for Deke, drums in the Deke Squad and is killed; a helper, and his girlfriend Tawni has no file.
Only on screen in The One Who Will Save Us All, where he refuses Talbot a seat and is absorbed into him; a Confederacy member with a few lines in Talbot's story.
Only in One of Us, but he is one of the episode's villains: Cal's team breaks him out and his scream attack on the school field is the threat Coulson stops.
On screen in six season 6 episodes (6x01, 6x04, 6x07, 6x09, 6x10, 6x13).
On screen in two season 2 episodes: ...Ye Who Enter Here (gets Bobbi the fort plans) and What They Become (passes her the theater note).
Only in Parting Shot (mentioned in Hot Potato Soup), but the episode turns on him: he is the Prime Minister Androvich's coup targets, and his choice to free Bobbi and Hunter decides how it ends.
On screen in two season 7 episodes (Stolen, Brand New Day).
Only in Devils You Know (mentioned later), but he is the case the episode is about: Lash's Inhuman tracker, whom the team catches and questions, and whom Lash kills.
On screen only in the Bahrain flashbacks of Melinda, where she is the Inhuman May fights and kills, and she is the mother of Katya Belyakova, who has a file.
On screen in two season 7 episodes (A Trout in the Milk, Adapt or Die).
Only on screen in Missing Pieces (a photo and mentions later), where he helps Keller with the ley lines and is shot by Sarge; a colleague with a few lines.
Only in One of Us, where he is the muscle on Cal's team who opens Brynmore's gates and fights May; a henchman in Cal's story, and Cal is his leader, not the other way round.
On screen in Meet the New Boss as the ghost who traps Mack and in the Momentum Labs flashback of The Good Samaritan.
Only in Fun & Games, where he is a bidder at Kasius's auction whom Fitz knocks out; a guest in Kasius's story.

Only in Rise and Shine, where in one flashback scene he hands Hale the Confederacy project and bites a cyanide pill; a minor part in Hale's backstory, and the wiki calls him her colleague, not her commander.
Only in Alien Commies from the Future!, where the team drugs and questions him about Area 51 and fakes an alien abduction; a witness in a side plot, and his wife has no file.
Only in Stolen, where he runs Malick's power-transfer machine at Afterlife; a helper in Malick's story.
On screen in two season 5 episodes (Fun & Games, The Last Day).
Only in The Writing on the Wall, but he is the T.A.H.I.T.I. subject Derik is after, the target the episode's climax is about, and he cuts Coulson free.
Only in Repairs, an episode that turns on her: the team's case is Hannah, blamed for the StatiCorp blast and haunted by Tobias Ford, and her words to him end it.
